facets.description: Google CalendarService reads res?.data, which a raw fetch Response lacks, so token.access_token throws and the refresh fails silently
zoho-bigin CalendarService reads tokenInfo.data.error on a fetch Response, causing a TypeError
zohocrm CalendarService reads zohoCrmTokenInfo.data.error on a fetch Response, causing a TypeError
Hubspot CalendarService treats the fetch Response as a HubspotToken and reads token fields it does not have, which corrupts the credential
Lark CalendarService passes the response to handleLarkError, which expects the provider envelope {code, msg, data} that the sync body lacks
Webex VideoApiAdapter expects provider-specific token fields (refresh-token fields) that are missing from the sync body

answer.reasoning: The group problem lists six affected callers: Google, the two Zoho apps, Hubspot, Lark and Webex. I did not make Office365 or Zoom their own facets, for three reasons. The group problem does not name them. Two members (s_678d253e and s_db4ed3db) say outright that these callers can work. And in the diff, zoom and office365calendar validate through parseRefreshTokenResponse, which uses the minimal schema in sync mode. s_514b72cc mentions office365/zoom only as background for why no single response shape works, so that mention does not change its status: it states all six facets and is complete. s_e502d1e6 names hubspot, the Zoho apps, google, lark and webex, and says each of these refresh flows breaks, so it is complete too. s_678d253e covers google, hubspot and both Zoho apps, but it explicitly says lark and webex can work, so it misses F5 and F6. s_db4ed3db covers only Google. Labeler 2's extra facets F7–F9 (Office365 and Zoom) go beyond what the group problem and the diff support.
